rules.instruction: When the description states that an external participant performs an action that initiates work by another participant: Model the action as a task in the external participant’s process and connect it to the receiving participant’s process with a message flow.
rules.situation: the description explicitly states that one participant sends information or an item to another participant to initiate subsequent work

rules.instruction: When the description explicitly identifies the role or participant responsible for an activity: Include that responsible role or participant in the BPMN activity label when needed to preserve who performs the work.
rules.situation: the description explicitly identifies who performs an activity, and omitting that participant from the activity label would make the performer unclear

rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity's result or a condition determines which of multiple alternative paths follows: Connect the activity to an exclusive gateway and model each alternative as a separate outgoing branch.
rules.situation: the description states that one of several mutually exclusive outcomes or actions will occur

rules.instruction: When the description says that an actor sends or forwards an item to another actor, but does not describe message communication as the work being performed: Model the action as an ordinary task rather than inferring a send-task subtype from the sending verb alone; use a send task when the description establishes that sending a message is itself the modeled work.
rules.situation: the description says that an actor sends or forwards an item to another actor, but does not describe message communication as the work being performed
